name: Texas

agency.name: Texas Department of Insurance, Division of Workers' Compensation (TDI-DWC)

ttd.rateText: Temporary income benefits (TIBs) equal 70% of the difference between the average weekly wage and post-injury weekly earnings; 75% for the first 26 weeks if the employee earns less than $10 an hour (Tex. Labor Code § 408.103).
ttd.minText: Minimum weekly income benefit is 15% of the state average weekly wage, rounded to the nearest dollar (§ 408.062); the maximum TIB is 100% of the SAWW, rounded (§ 408.061). The minimum in effect on the date of injury applies for the whole claim.
ttd.periodLabel: Texas fiscal year 2027: injuries from October 1, 2026 to September 30, 2027 (SAWW $1,314.32). For FY2026 (10/01/25-09/30/26): max $1,271.00, min $191.00.

waiting.text: Income benefits are not paid for an injury that does not cause disability for at least one week; benefits accrue on the eighth day of disability, and if disability lasts two weeks or longer, compensation is computed from the date disability begins (Tex. Labor Code § 408.082).

ttdDuration.text: TIBs continue until maximum medical improvement (§ 408.102); MMI is reached at the latest on the expiration of 104 weeks from the date income benefits begin to accrue (§ 401.011(30)), unless extended for spinal surgery under § 408.104.

ppd.text: Impairment income benefits (IIBs) start the day after MMI and are paid 3 weeks for each percentage point of impairment (§ 408.121) at 70% of the AWW (§ 408.126), capped at 70% of the SAWW (§ 408.061(b)): $920.00 a week in FY2027. Workers with a 15% or higher impairment rating who have not returned to work at 80% of their AWW may then receive supplemental income benefits (§ 408.142).

facts.text: Workers' compensation coverage is elective for private employers in Texas: except for public employers, an employer may elect to obtain coverage (Tex. Labor Code § 406.002), so employees of non-subscribers are not covered by the system.
Eligibility for temporary, impairment and supplemental income benefits ends 401 weeks after the date of injury (§ 408.083).
Texas maximums and minimums change on October 1 each year (state fiscal year), not on January 1; for FY2027 the state average weekly wage is $1,314.32.
Low-wage workers earning less than $10 an hour receive 75% instead of 70% of lost wages for the first 26 weeks of TIBs (§ 408.103(a)(2)).
